name: Glassmorphism

lumenary.blurb: Frosted glass panels floating over your picture.

why: Frosted glass is a window that hides detail but keeps colour. Put a translucent panel over a vivid picture and the panel inherits its hues while staying calm enough to hold text. This treatment builds that effect from layers: a soft shadow, a blurred copy of the picture, a tint, a diagonal sheen and a fine border that catches light on two corners.
how: Blur the picture by shrinking it by an amount set by the frost slider and enlarging it back in doublings with smoothing.
Draw a soft shadow, then clip to a rounded rectangle for each panel.
Inside the panel draw the blurred picture, then a translucent tint, white for light glass or near black for smoke.
Add a diagonal sheen that fades from bright to nothing.
Draw a one pixel border whose brightness varies along the diagonal, and place panels from a fixed layout nudged by the seed.
history: Translucent interface glass appeared in Windows Vista’s Aero in 2006 and 2007, and Apple’s iOS 7 in 2013 used blur behind panels. The designer Michal Malewicz popularised the name glassmorphism around 2020, when macOS Big Sur and many apps and websites adopted frosted cards.
uses: Cards for music and weather screens
terms: A filter that removes fine detail and keeps only broad shapes, which is what blur does.
A soft highlight across a surface.
The standard rule for laying a translucent layer over another.
paragraphs: Frosted glass is a blurred copy of the picture shown through a window. To get a smooth blur without an expensive convolution, the picture is shrunk by a factor that depends on the frost slider and then enlarged back in successive doublings with smoothing on. Each shrink throws away fine detail, and each smooth enlargement spreads what is left, which is a low-pass filter: the more it shrinks, the lower the cutoff and the stronger the frost.

Each panel is then built in layers. A soft shadow is drawn first. The panel shape is a rounded rectangle, used as a clip, inside which the blurred picture is drawn, then a translucent tint (white for light glass, near-black for smoke) mixed in by the “over” operator, then a diagonal sheen gradient that fades from bright to nothing, and finally a one-pixel border whose brightness varies along the diagonal so the glass seems to catch light on two corners. The panels’ positions are a fixed layout nudged by a seeded random offset, so “Rearrange” always gives a new but reproducible composition.

equations.note: Down-scale factor for frost amount b (0 to 100). The blurred layer is built at f × the picture size.
Tint over blur, with α = opacity × 0.55 for light glass.
Corner radius is a fraction of the shorter side.

presets.text: Smoked glass with strong frost reads as a dark mode card.
One large panel is a clean frame for a title.
Low frost keeps the picture clear behind the glass.
